This harbour is open very much longer in the year than any others on that side of Cape Breton. It is frequented during the season by seventy-nine sailing vessels on an average, averaging 80 tons each.
Are there not private wharfs at both these ports ?

There are no private wharfs at Port Hastings. I may say that that is the only point where large steamers along the eastern Nova Scotia coast can at all seasons secure bunker coal. A case in point is that of the steamship ' Bruce ' on the Newfoundland and Sydney route, which was obliged to come all the

way around eastern Cape Breton, leaving the Sydneys and Louisburg, and come to Port Hastings in order to secure bunker coal at the Inverness Railway Company's terminus. At such a port the public would naturally seek wharf accommodation. There was but an old government wharf there, built by the government of Nova Scotia before confederation. The Dominion government took this wharf over, but when the Inverness Coal and Railway Company was building its terminals at this point, it very largely covered over this wharf, and practically rendered it useless to the public. This rendered imperative either the extension of this old wharf or the construction of a new one. Hence the present vote. With regard to Port Hawkesbury, this is also a most important port. It is frequented by a large amount of shipping, both foreign and domestic, being a most capacious harbour. There are private wharfs at Port Hawkesbury, but very large steamers frequent the port, such as the Plant Dine, which cannot properly be accommodated at any of the private wharfs now available. The public, therefore, have urged upon me to impress upon the government the necessity of building a public wharf, which would not only accommodate the public, but also this very important line of steamers which make Port Hawkesbury their only port of call from the time they leave Halifax until they reach Charlottetown, P.E.I., and further I believe that the revenue to be realized from that wharf would more than repay the government for the interest on the cost.
What would be the probable revenue from the wharf ?
Between $700 and $800 a year. There would be $500 from that line of steamers alone.
How much revenue was there last year ?
The wharf is not built yet.
I understood from the hon. gentleman that one of these wharfs was owned by the government and that it was taken possession of and covered up by a railway company. Is that correct ?
Very largely.
Did the government collect from the company anything for the filling up of that wharf ?
No doubt the Department of Railways and Canals will see to that matter.

Have they already done so? Did the government allow a railway company simply to come in and cover up a government wharf without any arrangement having been previously come to between that company and the government, or if any Mr. McLennan.
amount was paid to the government, when was it paid and how much?
I have no information with regard to any claim against the company. Probably this wharf had not been kept in repair and was not very valuable.

I understand that the government purchased a wharf, and expended a very large amount of money on it and then, after some years had elapsed, simply allowed a railway company to come and take possession of it and fill it up. The hon. member for Inverness made that statement.
My hon. friend said that the province of Nova Scotia, previous to confederation, had a wharf there. I did not understand him to say that this government had ?
I understood him to say that the Dominion government took the wharf over.
I shall have an inquiry made into the matter and bring down all the particulars.
Perhaps the hon. member for Inverness will repeat what he did say.

I said that the government of Nova Scotia had built this wharf before confederation, and that the Dominion goverment took it over, and 'that subsequently Messers Mackenzie and Mann built their railway and terminals over and across the wharf, and thus rendered it useless to the public.
Is this in the hon. gentleman's constituency ?
Yes.
Did the hon. gentleman draw the attention of the department to what this railway has done ?
I considered that the Department of Railways and Canals would no doubt see to that matter.
Then the hon. gentleman did complain to the department ?
I did not say that I complained to any department, because I did not, but I said that I had no doubt the Railway Department had entered into some negotiations with this railway company.

Then the railway company went in and took possession of government property without any arrangement at all between it and the government, and after that had been done, the hon. member representing the county drew the attention of the government to the fact. Is that what happened ?

The hon. gentleman has said that he has no doubt the department will make the railway company pay for the damage they have done to this wharf, but he says he did not report the matter to the department. How then can he say he has no doubt as to what the department will do ?

The Department of Railways had steam communication between Mulgrave and that wharf, and in fact had this wharf as one of the terminals of the Intercolonial Railway until the Inverness and Richmond Railway was built, and I have no doubt that before the Department of Railways allowed this wharf to go to any private corporation some consideration was secured.
Sandy Cove-breakwater, $13,200.
This work is under contract. The amount of the contract is $13,000 and the contractors are Hayden & Oliver, Digby. It is estimated that the work will cost $14,300.
What is the necessity for this work ?

These are piers for the benefit of the fishing people of the district. It is well known that this is one of the best fishing districts in the province, and there are many men with a large fleet of boats engaged in this industry. The bait freezer has been erected at this place recently.
Short Beach-breakwater, $8,000.
This is in Yarmouth county. The work is under contract for $8,095. The total cost is $9,000.
Is this for the purpose of creating a harbour of shelter ?

Yes. A harbour of shelter for fishermen.
South Ingonish-wharf, $1,800.

This work is under contract for $2,485. The total estimated cost of the work is $2,800.
Three Fathom harbour-restoration of beach protection works, $1,200.
What county is this in 7
Halifax.
Will this complete the work 7

It is estimated that this will complete it.
Tiverton-breakwater, $17,000.
Was the lowest tenderer accepted in this case ?

Yes, this was let to the lowest tenderer.
Washabuck Centre-wharf, $5,500.
This is a new wharf. The amount of the contract is $5,860 and $6,500, it is estimated, will complete the work.
What is the necessity for the expenditure ?

This wharf is built for the convenience of a large class of farmers on the Bras d'Or lakes. The steamer passes up and down in front of this place three times a week, from Why-cocomagh and Baddeck to the Sydneys. This will enable the farmers to hare a port of call there for the steamer, to ship their produce and receive the goods that they get in. This has been promised them for many years, but I happened to be the one who was able to bring the promise into effect.
West Baccaro-boat harbour protection and channel, $3,500.
What is this for 7
For the protection of shipping.
What is the channel ?
It is to have a depth of three feet.
What does it connect with ?
It connects with the Atlantic Ocean.
I know; but what does it connect the Atlantic Ocean with 7
I am afraid my knowledge of the locality is somewhat limited, I shall have to ask the member for the riding to explain.

All along that coast there are small ponds shut off by beaches from the sea, and by making channels you are able to let the fishermen take in their boats and so assure them of protection during the storms. This is a fishing settlement a short distance from port Latour. The whole district is a fishing district. It is some years since I was there, and the young men pointed out the disadvantage they laboured under owing to the destruction of their boats during the storms. For a small sum of money, you can give them protection for their fishing boats.
Has any investigation been made as to the depth of the pond with which the channel is to connect ?
I presume that the engineers must have a report.
Is this a local work Intended for the protection of local boats ?
Yes, fishing boats.
Why not apply the same principle all over the maritime provinces and build local works for the protection of local boats wherever required ?
Wherever any case of that kind

I made out some very good cases in this House. And I contend that where you build a harbour for the protection of local fishermen in the province of Nova Scotia, you ought to do the same in the province of Prince Edward Island or New Brunswick.
Or Quebec.

Yes, or Ontario or any other province. The case I have made out in this parliament was of ponds or lakes around the coast of Prince Edward Island that would afford accommodation not only to the fishermen of the locality, but also the fishermen of Nova Scotia or New Brunswick plying their avocation on those shores. But I think it strange that a sum of money should be voted by parliament for the purpose simply of making a harbour for local fishermen.

I agree that there should be no sectionalism in the matter. If this is a sound policy in any place, it is equally sound in any other. There is nothing new in the case. We are doing here a work such as has been done in Nova Scotia for many years, and it is a most useful class of work, notwithstanding what hon. gentlemen may say to the contrary. In no way can you render more useful service to the fishermen along the Atlantic coast than by providing them with harbours for their boats. If we neglect this these men will be driven away from the coast and will be unable to carry on their operations. My hon. friend from Lunenburg (Mr. Kaulbach) who represents a great fishing county, understands the matter well, and I am sure he will agree with me. Of course, if there is any other portion of the coast under similar conditions in any other province, it has the same claim and the same right to consideration.

There seems to be varied requirements in the maritime provinces. As I understand it, in the province of Nova Scotia, if a pond is adjoining the ocean it is deemed advisable to make a strait or canal to connect the two so that it may be made a harbour of refuge. When you come to the adjoining province of Prince Edward Island we find directly the reverse, because we find at Cascumpec harbour that an opening through the beach is closed. It would seem that in Prince
Edward Island there was a pond inside, but there was the wild raging ocean outside, so the department are going to close up the breach so that the rough tide cannot get into the still waters.

Both these cases are eminently proper. In the one case a break in the beach would do great harm, and you close the beach in the interest of the protection of the people who are engaged in fishing. In the other case, owing to the storms, you need to cut the channel to allow boats to have access to shelter. Both cases are right and reasonable.
There is one case, Port Bruce, where they have asked for the same favour and were refused.

I have never heard of such an application ; of course it would not come before me. All I can say is that in my judgment there should be no sectionalism. If there is a case of a similar kind in any part of Canada where we can protect our fishermen and keep them at home, these improvements should be made in their interest. If these small expenditures will help to make their lives easy and help them in their business, I am in favour of making them.

The fishermen at Port Bruce are paying a license to the department, and when they asked for this improvement the Public Works Department tell them, ' No, go to the Marine Department.' It is not a benefit for the accommodation of the fisTiermen only.

Would the minister say whether there has been any investigation made to ascertain the depth of the pond ? Of course it would be of no use to cut a channel to this pond unless you know something about the depth of the water.
A memorandum furnished me says there are three feet of water.
Three feet of water will carry fishing boats easily.
Is that at high tide or low tide ?
At low tide.
That seems pretty small but I suppose it may be of some little service.

I agree with the Minister of Finance regarding expenditures of this kind. Along the shores of Nova Scotia particularly, there are places of this sort where expenditures like this are needed for the protection of boats. I know that along the shore of Halifax county with which

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: I am familiar, as well as in my own county and the adjoining county, there are places of this sort.

With regard to Cas-eumpee harbour, I wish to say that it is the resort of shipping from all parts of the gulf of St. Lawrence and from the Atlantic ocean. It is a deep water harbour. This channel opening through a sand hill was made by freshets and high tides, and the engineer no doubt felt it his duty to have this closing filled up in order that a gi eater volume of water might flow through the main channel. Cascumpec harbour is one of the most important harbours on the north shore of Prince Edward Island. It does not accommodate merely the people of the locality, but as I say, is a resort for shipping from all parts of Canada and the world.
At six o'clock, the committee took recess.
After Recess.
Committee resumed at eight o'clock.
Belfast pier-dredging, $1,750.
This is a revote. May I ask the hon. minister why this amount was not expended last year ?

The reason this work was not done was that there was no dredge available. There is one small dredge which the department hcis for that purpose, but it was working in another part of the island, I understand, all last season. We hope we may be able to go on with this work.
Will the dredge be placed there next year ?

I do not know whether I will be able to give the hon. gentleman (Mr. Hackett) a definite promise, but I hope to be able to arrange for the work going on during next year.
Cascumpec harbour-closing opening through beach, $1,500.
I would like to ask the hon. minister what has been done in that connection within the last year, or what is going on now in regard to the closing of the outlet from the main harbour to the ocean.
The work is now going on, the materials have been procured and it is proposed that, this work shall be completed before the 30th June next.
Is it being done by contract or by day labour ?
It is being done by day labour.

Who is the foreman of the work going on now and what is the 37
quantity of material which has been placed there-how many loads of brush and stone ?
I have not the name of the foreman, but I shall be very pleased to bring down a statement showing who the foreman is who is in charge of this work.

I think this is an item which does not come under the class of work described as repairs. The hon. minister ought to be in a position to explaiu to the committee why it is that this cannot be let by tender. It looks to me as if it could be very well let by tender.

There are two openings here, and it is desirable to close one of them. The hon. member for Prince West (Mr. Hackett) will know the locality and the reasons for this expenditure better than I do myself. I have the report of the engineer of the department and it shows that this work is necessary to provide better harbour accommodation.
Is this the total estimated expenditure ?
This finishes the work. It is all to be completed, we hope, before the 30th of June next.

We have had the same statement for some years aud yet the thing is going on. I suppose the hon. minister is quite sincere in his statement now that this will conclude the work, and that before an election takes place there will be nothing going on in this direction. My experience has been that around election time we will find work of this kind going on. We have the money voted year after year, there is nothing done until just about election time when the money is placed in the hands of parties who will carry out the desires of the government. I think this is wrong especially in the province of Prince Edward Island where these works are of a very important character. They should be attended to without party spirit or party influence of any kind. I trust the hon. minister will see that this work at Cascumpec that has been hanging on for so many years will be completed in a short time.

It may be possible that governments are [DOT]guilty on some occasions, but I do not think on this particular occasion they are guilty of using this work for political purposes. That appropriation, I think, was made for the first time after the election in my hon. friend's county so that it could not have been to purchase his support there. I am speaking from the report of the engineer of the department. The material has been purchased, the work will be proceeded with and the greater part of it will he completed, I have no doubt. I have no reason to believe that statement is not correct.

This matter has been under consideration for a number of years. We have discussed it here before. This opening through the sandhills from Cascum-pec harbour occurred some years ago and an estimate was made for closing up the channel. Year after year we have been discussing the necessity of closing this channel and I trust now that the hon. minister will see that the matter will be concluded and that we will have no more of this difficulty.

I will try to see that the work is proceeded with quickly.
Cove head harbour-improvement of entrance channel, $4,000.
What is the meaning of that ?
This is a revote of $4,000 of the previous vote and with the amount to be expended before the 30th of June it will make the total cost $7,300. This work is now under contract.
When was this contract let ?
It was let on the 13th of March last.
This is an entirely new work ?

Yes.
Creosoted timber for piers and breakwaters, $2,000.
I would like to ask the hon. minister where these piles are purchased, what they cost and who provides them ?
This is a general vote for creosoted wood required for piles throughout the province of Prince Edward Island. The wood is purchased at Norfolk, Virginia.
What amount was purchased last year ?

There was no creosoted timber purchased for Prince Edward Island last year.
Gaspereaux-harbour for fishermen in Graham's Pond, $500?
What is the meaning of* this ?
This is for necessary repairs to the harbour during the year.
What kind of a harbour is it ? It is for local fishermen ?
Yes, it seems to be for the use of fishermen particularly.
What is the value of the improvements made there ? Have you improved the harbour very much by the expenditure provided by this parliament ?
Does my hon. friend mean the public expenditure to date, or the amount that we require now ? This $500 is all that we are asking for
Did you not spend an amount there before ? There was money spent there before.
I find that $500 was spent there during the past year and this $500 completes the work.
What is the improvement made by this ?
It is to protect the channel opened from the sea to Graham's pond, to permit the fishing boats to enter the pond at all times of tide.

The total expenditure cn this work will be, I understand, $1,000. I submit that this is not the class of work that this parliament should engage in. When a work is of such trifling character as only to amount to $1,000 it cannot be within the province of this parliament to expend that money.
You must not expend anything as small as $1,000.

Probably not, and I will explain it from my point of view, which may not be that of the Postmaster General. I submit I will have the judgment of the majority of the people of this country; the people who ought to be our masters; the people who contribute the money for us to expend, when I say that a trifling work like this, is a matter for the municipality, or at most, for the province, if it is a public work at all. Where is the line to be drawn ? If we are to pick out here and there through Canada trifling little works in which any man of enterprise would engage as a private venture upon his own capital, where are we going to draw the line, in asking the parliament of Canada to vote for such works If this be the rule, then there are thousands, nay, there are hundreds of thousands of spots in this Dominion which are entitled to the expenditure of public money, and it would be better, far better because it would be far more honest if the federal government would in that case take upon itself the entire expenditure of all the moneys that are required by the people of this country. Surely there is some line of demarcation between what is the duty of the provincial legislature and what is the duty of the federal administration, fl'liat is the point I want to make notwithstanding the interjection of the Postmaster General.

These small works, if they are of a public nature at all, must be within the expenditure of the local municipality or within the expenditure of the province. I do not mean that federal works must permeate every part of the Dominion, but they must be, to some extent, of that large national character, as distinguished from a local character, before they can be entitled to draw contribution from the people of this entire Dominion. Notwithstanding the jocular interjection of the Postmaster General, I submit that such an expenditure as this is not justifiable. When this matter comes to be considered as it will be considered; when it comes to be discussed as it will be discussed on the hustings, it will be the almost universal voice of the people of Canada regardless of political affinities that that is the true basis upon which we must proceed as trustees of the money of the people of this country.

This pond is one of great importance I believe to the fishermen. About the year 1900 operations commenced there for the opening of the harbour, and at the same time the operations commenced at Skinner's pond in Prince county a month before the election, and a large number of men were employed. The Skinners pond work has been dropped because the people there voted against the government. I now ask the minister is it his intention to continue the work at Skinner's pond in Prince county, the same as at Gaspereaux, in King's county, or is it the intention of the government to let it lie until the election approaches ?

Skinner's pond has not been brought to my attention and evidently there was no work done there previous to the election. I can hardly agree with my hon. friend (Mr. Lennox) about these small works, because they must be of great importance to the community or else representations would not be made by the people and their representatives in these districts to have these works carried out. It is not fair to say that they are private works because as a matter of fact they are for the benefit of the fishing community who are engaged in an important industry in this country. If my hon. friend were to visit the maritime provinces I am quite sure he would change his views. I am not prepared to say that because we spend .$100,000 or $200,000 on a pier to accommodate extensive shipping, that the fishing industry of Canada should not be provided with facilities to carry on its business. It is necessary to afford shelter along the shores of Prince Edward Island, Nova Scotia and New Brunswick, and it is tire province of this parliament to provide for that.

Let me point out the fallacy of that argument. The revenue of tile'fisheries has been given to the provinces by decision of the Privy Council. No doubt 371
the minister is perfectly correct in saying that this work is of great importance to the fishermen in that locality, but where is there a public work of which it cannot be said that it is of special importance to a particular class of the people. It would be of great importance to a large section of the people of Toronto if a pier was built there, and I am told there is no government pier in Toronto. Now, I would argue against doing such a work in Toronto in the same way, if it could not be shown that the influence of that expenditure extended beyond the city of Toronto. The moneys which this parliament administers are to be administered in the interests of Canada as a whole, and when yon talk of a work being of vast interest to a particular body of fishermen, you are speaking only of a number of people in a small locality. When you talk of this being of advantage to a body of fishermen, you speak of a work for a small locality just as you would speak of a work for a township or a county. I submit that if the benefit of an expenditure does not extend beyond the radius of a small community, even though it is somewhat densly settled, there is no justification for it. Go to the city of Hamilton or the town of Barrie or the village of Bradford, which is represented by the hon. Postmaster General. There are many people in the village of Bradford and in the locality of Lake Sim-coe who would be vastly benefited by the dredging of the Holland river. They would tell you that it would serve a large number of farmers on either side of the lake, and that it would increase the commerce of the thriving village of Bradford. We have not had any request for such an expenditure. Whether we shall, on the eve of an election, God only knows ; but we have not had it yet, and I submit that an expenditure would be as justifiable in the one case as in the other. I will not trouble the committee any more on this question for the present; but I have endeavoured to point out that there is a broad distinction between an expenditure which may be said to be in the general interests of the people we represent, and those purely local concerns which should be aided and assisted, if at all, by the local government.

What is the distinction between Skinner's pond and Graham's pond ? In the year 1900 there was a vote for improvements at Graham's pond, and in the same year certain improvements were made at Skinner's pond without any appropriation, but after the election nothing more was done. Now, I find that the government are prosecuting the improvement of Graham's pond while leaving Skinner's pond without any appropriation at all. What is the reason of this ? Is it because the people in the neighbourhood of Skinner's pond returned an opponent of the goTernment. while the people in the neighbourhood of Graham's pond supported a man to uphold the government ?
We would not do anything like that.

I am sure you did. The work was commenced about a month before the election of 1900. When I found In going through the country that the work was commenced, I was astonished, because there was no appropriation for it by this parliament; but I wastoldi that the money was taken from the general appropriation for public works. I had to light against that. The government purchased many votes by this work. But after the election, the work was dropped, and no work lias gone on since at Skinner's pond. I ask, in the name of the people of Prince county, that the government will prosecute the work at Skinner's pond just as they are doing at Graham's pond.
Higgin's shore pier-works of reconstruction and repair, $1,000.
May I ask the hon. minister to explain this item ?
This is a revote. It is for the purpose of repairing the wharf.
Why was the money not expended last year ?
There were some representations made in regard to the change of site, but the engineer thought it best that the old pier should be repaired. That is the cause of the delay.

I want to say in all seriousness that the expenditure of $1,000 on the old pier would be simply a waste of money. A new pier should be built about 100 yards east of the old pier, and I would ask the hon. minister if, in addition to this vote, he will place an appropriation in the supplementary estimates to build a completely new pier.

On the report of the engineer it is estimated that this $1,000 will put the work in good shape. We have a detailed estimate of what is required. But, in view of the representation made by the hon. gentleman, I will ask the engineer to make a further report on the work.

Has the hon. minister received a petition from that part of Prince county on this subject ? If he wants to give satisfaction to the people of the locality he will build a new pier.
Lower Montague-Altken's wharf, $2,800.
Mr-. HACKETT. What is being done there ?
The MINISTER OF PUBLIC WORj^S. This is for completing the work. The total estimated cost is $4,500.
New London-repairs to breakwater, &e., $500.
I would like to draw the minister's attention to page Y-225, which states that the contract here is completed. If so, what do you want this money for ?

My hon. friend will see that this vote is for repairs required during the next year. In reply to the hon. gentleman I beg to say that the engineer estimates $500 will be required for the repairs of this pier and that is why we are asking the money. Every hon. gentleman must know that these piers are liable to injury through storms and ice and so on, and require considerable repairs to keep them from going to pieces.
Last year this breakwater appears to have been thoroughly repaired and there would seem to be some particular cause for this new expenditure.
Some $446 were spent on repairs on this wharf last year, and the engineer reports $500 are required to keep it in repair for the coming year.
There were spent last year $5,701.61 for completing the work.
That was for building the breakwater.
No, for repairs.
That must be a misprint.

If the work were built last year why should it require repairs this year 7 That appears to be too quick altogether. It may be that the expenditure last year was for repairs, as the structure was standing some years, but if we built a new work last year we should not be called on to repair it this year.

I desire to point out that this work last year was all repairs, as the hon. minister will see by referring to V-225 of the Auditor General's Report. It is headed ' repairs to breakwater, &c.' and Includes $5,493 paid T. B. Cullen to complete contract, but that was a contract, not for building but for repairs. Then there are payments to the inspector of work and for advertising, &c., and the total is carried to page Y-7 under the heading ' repairs to breakwater, New London.'

If my hon. friend will look on page 62 of the report of the Public Works Department, he will find a full explanation of this work. This $500 is for repairs necessary owing to damages done to the pier by storms since the reconstruction was completed.
Repairs to piers and breakwaters, Prince Edward Island, $6,000.
Will tlie lion, minister give us some idea of these repairs ?

This is the annual vote for general repairs. It has been the practice of parliament for many years to vote $6,000 for general re-jiairs to piers and breakwaters in Trince Edward Island, not provided for by special vote. Up to the first of March, 1903, we spent $1,240 of last year's vote. This money of course is not expended unless absolutely required to keep the piers and wharfs in repair, which are not otherwise provided for by special vote.

The Auditor General's Report shows that last year there was spent out of the $6,000, $1,554.63. This year the [DOT]hon. minister tells us that $1,240 has been silent so far. That would leave the difference between $1,240 and $6,000 to be stili expended.
That $4,760 lapses on the 30th June if not expended.

Perhaps the members from Prince Edward Island may ask for works in the meantime to be done, which will absorb this money.
The MINISTER OF PUBLIC WORKS, l'ou cannot expend this money except for the purposes for which it is appropriated, and the department will not expend it unless it be really necessary for repairs to piers and breakwaters.

I may say that this money which was voted last year should be all expended because those piers belonging to the government are falling into disrepair. Hon. gentlemen may think it is a great thing to vote $6,000 and expend only $1,200 out of that vote, but the piers and wharfs along the shores of Prince Edward Island which belong to the government, are falling into disrepair because money is not expended on them to keep them in good order. I have every confidence in Mr. Hogan, the engineer down there, but no doubt his instructions are to save every dollar he can for the government. But the government are in this respect too saving. They vote the money and make the peoifie believe that they are spending it, but instead they spend it in some other part of Canada and the island has its piers and breakwaters falling to pieces. I would like to ask the hon. minister if he intends spending the whole of this vote of $6,000 this year on the wharfs and breakwaters in Prince Edward Island.
The MINISTER OF PUBLIC WORKS As I have explained, this money is spent upon the report of the engineer. I am pleased to know that we have an economical man, but sorry to hear that he would allow these works to go to pieces when the
money is voted to keep them in repair. It is not likely that the engineer who represents the department in Prince Edward Island .would allow the state of affairs to exist which my hon. friend represents, especially when he knows that the money lias been voted to make the repairs required. If we only spent $1,600 the year before and $1,240 so far this year, it was not because the department was not willing to spend the money but because no reports came to us from the engineer that the work was necessary. The money voted for this purpose could not be spent in any other part of the island or of Canada for any other purpose. It simply lapses and is not spent at all.

But suppose the hon. gentleman from West Prince (Mr. Hackett) went to the department and asked to have this work done, the hon. minister might say there was no money for the purpose. But when we find that there is an unexpended balance of $6,000 that would be hardly a fair statement of facts. Perhaps the hon. gentleman would say whether he applied to the department and was told there was no money for the purpose.

I do not think so.
Souris, Knight's Point - strengthening of breakwater, $10,000.

This is for the placing of large stones on the seaward side of the breakwater at Knight's Point, filling in with ordinary sized ballast, depressions in the body of the crib-work, and making general repairs, &c. There will be needed two thousand cubic yards of large stone, and one thousand cubic feet of ordinary ballast. The general repairs to the cribwork will cost over $1,000; in all $10,000.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
speechtext: Is this under contract, awarded after calling for tender ?
Yes.
What is the contract price?

Seventy-four cents per cubic yard. The contractor is J. Lanigan.
Tignish-rebuilding northern breakwater, $700.
Will the hon. gentleman explain the meaning of this item ?
This is to be applied to the building up of a block on the breakwater which has settled about three feet.

This Tignish breakwater has been but lately completed, and why are we now asked to spend this amount ? And is it the intention of the government

to call for tenders, or will this be done by day's work ?

I suppose that this work being in the hou. gentleman's own constituency, he would be familiar with the conditions. A report was received from the engineer, of whom I have no personal knowledge, but whom I understand to be a very good man. I have already explained what is to be done with the money. If this work is not done the block will be very seriously affected in a short time.
What kind of work is intended ?
As I understand, this is for rebuilding the superstructure of the cribwork, which originally cost $4,500.

Is it the intention to drive piles around the breakwaters ?
The MIlAsTER OF PUBLIC WORKS. No, stone.

Before leaving the Prince Edward Island items, I would like to ask the Minister of Public Works what is being done in Summerside with regard to the works prosecuted there some years ago, and on which operations were being carried on up to a very late date ? And have the contractors been paid off ?

I shall be obliged to look into that matter. There is no vote here for Summerside, and I have no particulars at hand. I would rather bring down full particulars for my hon. friend than attempt to speak from memory. I believe there is some difficulty about the matter, for I remember the subject being brought to my attention some time ago. I will have a memorandum made of the particulars and bring it down for the information of the hon. gentleman (Mr. Hackett).
About what time may we expect that ?

The hon. gentleman may have it when the supplementary estimates are under discussion or during next week.
New Brunswick-Anderson's Hollow-improvements and repairs to wharf, $1,800.
What about this ?

There was an appropriation of $6,500 for this work. The work is now under way and nearing completeness. We are asking a revote of $1,000 on the former vote and the new vote of $800 to complete the work.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
speechtext: Was it not let by tender ?
Was there not an estimate of cost for this work of $2,500 for last year 1
Not likely, because there was a vote of $6,500 last session.

But when that vote was asked for the minister said :
This vote is applied for to make provision for repairing the present pier, the estimated cost of which is $2,500 and also putting in a groin to overcome an accumulation of sand and gravel, estimated to cost $4,000.
So, the former estimate does not complete the work.

It was short by $800.
Bay du Vin-to complete reconstruction of wharf, $500.
What is the total cost of that work ?
The total is $12,847.64. This $500 will complete the work.
Was that done by contract ?

Yes.
Campbellton wharf-extension and repairs, $18,000.
May I ask the minister if this work has been commenced, and have tenders been asked for ?

I find that the late government had spent a sum of money on this property. It is private property, and belongs to Mr. Shives. It has been thought best by the department to purchase the property, the right of way, and have full control of this wharf. It is an important point, a great deal of shipping comes there, and it is necessary to maintain the wharf. There has been public money spent on this property previously, but I do not know how much.
When ?

A sum of $31,000 has been spent on this property previous to 1896, I cannot say now in what years it was spent. No money has been spent since 1896. Thej work now requires extension and improvements, and it is thought better to take the whole property over and have it vested in the Crown.

I find in the Auditor General's Report, page D-229, that $2,251 was spent on this work last year, apparently it was spent for odds and ends in the shape of labour, machines, pieces of timber and so forth. Now I think we ought to know whether a contract is going to be let, and whether this whole $18,000 is going to be spent in the same slipshod manner.

My hon. friend does not understand me. I said that an extension or addition had been biiilt to this wharf at considerable cost. The amount expended since 1896 has been for keeping the wharf In repair, that part belonging to the government. It is very unsatisfactory to have the adjoining property belonging to a private individual, and we propose to acquire that property.
What is hel going to do with the $18,000, how is it going to be handled ?
$15,000 of this will be devoted to purchasing the property belonging to Mr. Shives, the wharf and approaches belong to him. The $3,500 is for repairs.	-
Has the property been acquired from this man yet ?

No, there have been negotiations about the purchase, but we cannot make the purchase until we have the money voted. If the gentleman who owns the property will not transfer it to the Crown, of course the money will not be spent. The engineer thinks there is no binding contract, but there have been negotiations with the owner.
In what constituency is this ?
In the county of Itestigouche.
Will there be any revenue derived from this expenditure?
There will be considerable revenue, but we are not depending so much on the revenue as on the advantage this wharf will be to the public.
Will the hon. gentleman tell us what this land is worth, and how much, if any, Mr. Shives himself has expended on it.
We are negotiating for the purchase of that portion of the wharf that belongs to him.

We can get very little information about this whole transaction. There is no doubt the government have expended money on this property, and now they are buying it and paying a larger sum for it by reason of having expended money on it themselves. The property has been made more valuable by reason of the government money expended on it.

Whether the previous government made a good or a bad expenditure of money on this wharf, I believe it is good policy now to keep the work.in repair, and to purchase the property if we can get it at a reasonable price.
Will the minister tell us what certificate or what evidence he has that the price is a reasonable one ?

The department have certificates from their officers and reports as to the value of this property and the public necessity for it. We are certainly not buying it blindly. We are not asking for a vote for the purpose of buying it because it is not in the public interest.	It is because part of the wharf
belongs to the Crown and part to Mr. Shives-and it is desirable that this should be made public property. That is the object In negotiating for the purchase.
The hon. gentleman stated that the last government expended money on this property though the government did not own it. I inferred that from the hon. gentleman's remarks.
That is correct.
And now this government intends making an expenditure of money on this approach, and they intend to buy it.
Not on the approach, but on the part that has been previously built by the government.
How much land altogether is to be purchased ?
The land is only the approach to the wharf.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
speechtext: What quantity of land is in the approach ?

The wharf is built in front of a street in the town. It is not the land that we are purchasing; it is the wharf. The wharf was built by private enterprise, and it is owned by Mr. Shives. What we want to do is to secure the approach to the government wharf; that is to the wharf owned by the government previously. The hon. gentleman will see that the government having built an extension of the private wharf they cannot get over to their own property without going over the property of Mr. Shives.

Is it absolutely true that the late government paid money out to improve Mr. Shives' property without having any control over it, or is it not the fact that the last government expended money on the property that belongs to the Crown, and not on the approach ?
The MINISTER OF PUBLIC AVORIvS. There is no object in keeping anything back about this matter. There is no object in misrepresenting it. I did not tell the hon. gentleman that they spent it on the wharf that Mr. Shives had already built. I said that they had built an extension. I am only

speaking from the information given to me by the officers of the department, and I explained to the hon. gentleman that they had built an extension of this wharf at an expense of $31,000, and that the approach to this part of the wharf Mr. Shives owned and it still belongs to him. We want to purchase that and have the whole property vested in the Crown and make the repairs for which we are asking $3,100.
Has the hon. gentleman a plan of this work ?
Yes, in the department.
Will the hon. gentleman have any objection to laying it on the Table V
I will be very pleased to bring down the plan.
I think we understand it as far as the facts are concerned. There is a wharf built by the government. Between that and the land there is an approach owned by a private individual.
A wharf.

There is an approach in which a private individual is interested. Does this Mr. Shives own the whole of the approach or only a portion of it ?
The MINISTER OF PUBLIC WORKS, lie owns it all.
Now, I think it is very easy for the minister to tell us what land is covered by that approach ?
I will be pleased to bring down the plan to show the extent.
Cannot the hon. minister at present give us practically the dimensions of it ?
Perhaps the engineer has some information. The structure is 201 feet in length, 24 feet in width and there are 114 feet of water at low water.

Is the portion that belongs to Mr. Shives 294 feet in length and 24 feet in width and for which there is asked tne sum of $15,000 ? I have not made it up myself, but I am told that that is less than one-fifth of an acre of land. Is this a large city, or a town ? What kind of a place is it ? Do you know the population ?
It is quite an important place. I have tried to explain that we are not buying land, but the wharf-the structure.

I do not know what the hon. minister means, when he makes a distinction between buying land and buying the Hon. Mr. SUTHERLAND.
structure, that the structure, which is called the approach, was an expensive structure to build, blit I would say that when we hear of $15,000 for a work for which up to the present time we have had no claim made by Mr. Shives, it does suggest pretty strongly that this is a matter, at all events, requiring a good deal of looking into. We have had some trouble in dealing with the Expropriation Act and I think that the hon. minister ought to take very careful means of investigating this before he decides to put $15,000 into it and be very sure as to tlie title of Mr. Shives.
I may say as to the title, that that goes through the Department of Justice. I find that they are pretty strict about having a complete title.
I am told that the population is 2,000.

As to the value, I may say that in our experience in the past we have found, if we could make a fair arrangement according to the valuation put on property by our own officials, from the best information they could gather, that it has been preferable to going to the court and instituting expropriation proceedings. The experience of the Public Works Department is that by the time we pay the award, the lawyers fees and all the costs it would have paid us two or three times over to take the value put on the property by the officers of the department. The officers of the department have no object in the world in over-valuing these properties. They have no object in procuring them except in the public interest. If we think that a property is valued too high we can proceed under the Expropriation Act and refer it to the court. Unless we get property at the valuation put upon it by our own officials, appointed to value it, we generally apply to the court under expropriation proceedings.
How much has this property been estimated at ?

Fifteen thousand dollars.
I-Ion. Mr. TARTE. Have you the valuation there ?
The reports are in the department.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
speechtext:
If I understand the hon. minister correctly this pier or wharf is beside the water, so that there is no land to be acquired at all, and Mr. Shives now owns the piece of the wharf extending out into the ocean. At the end of his wharf the late government, I understand from the hon. minister, built an extension. Are we to assume that the late government went on and expended a lot of money building an ex-

tension to a wharf owned by a private individual ?
Yes, it did.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
speechtext: This is a matter which requires investigation. Did Mr. Shives own this property when the late government made the extension.
It was formerly owned by Mr. Ferguson, then by Mr. Mowatt and now by Mr. Shives, who I think has owned it for 20 years or more.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
speechtext: WTho was the owner when the late government made the extension ?
I would have to bring down a return to show all these dates. I have merely the facts given me by the department.
Will the minister allow this item to stand until we get the plan of the wharf.
I have no objection at all.

I visited this place and I know something about it. There was an existing wharf belonging to a private owner and the late government built a cross wharf at the end of that, but unfortunately they forgot to make arrangements with the owner of the wharf, so that in order to reach the government wharf you have to cross on private property.
They complain they are charged exliorbi-tant rates.
Yes, I tried several times to settle it and my recollection is that when I left office there was a report to council in favour of arbitration.

1 understand that is the least price they will accept, and it is a question as to whether we should expropriate and pay perhaps a higher price and all the costs. We know from past experience what that means.
Yes, I know it.

1 should think that after the explanation given the House will see that it is in the public interest that we should secure this property. The people complain that they have to pay exkorbitant rates to get to the government wharf and as there is a great deal of shipping done at this port it is desirable that this work should become the property of the Crown. None of this money will be paid until we have secured a proper title.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
speechtext:
I would certainly like to see the plans of the dock, because I can hardly imagine that the late government *made an expenditure there without having
some arrangement with the then owner of the property that the people should have a right to use it.
I have investigated that point and I can assure my hon. friend that there was no arrangement made at the time. However, as to the price let me say that I think that it is pretty high.
I think so too.

It is pretty high. The wharf belongs to Mr. Shives now who bought it some five or six years ago, and we are at his mercy to a large extent because our wharf cannot be used without passing on his property. For a time I contemplated building a wharf elsewhere but l found it would have cost more and so I resolved to go to arbitration. It was the last act I did on that question.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
speechtext:
The hon. gentleman (Hon.
I Mr Tarte) throws some light on this subject which confirms my opinion and bears out what I have heard. Mr. Shives acquired this property some five or six years ago. I am creditably informed that Mr. Shives is a strong supporter of the hon. gentlemen opposite and the ex-minister says that he thinks that it is a very big price to pay Mr. Shives. I think so too. This $15,000 will build an extension from the dock erected by the late government into the street, and he will have nothing to pay to Mr. Shives. I have a strong suspicion that the late government made an arrangement with the then owner of this property or they would not have been so foolish as to spend this money. It is said that in order to reach this government wharf the people have to pay toll. There is nothing extraordinary in that, for it is the case in connection with almost every wharf in Ontario. In my own town of Gananoque, if we want to ship anything we have to pay the Rath-bun Company to get on their wharfs to do our shipping. Why should the government to give free wharfs in one place and make the people pay for their wharf accommodation in another. Why, the revenues of some of these wharfs in the lower provinces is not sufficient to pay the salary of the wharfinger. In some cases we do not get $2 a year from wharfs which cost us thousands of dollars. Before this item ] insses I want to see the plan of the property, and who was the owner at the time the late government made this expenditure.

I am perfectly sure that no arrangement was made by the late government. As to that there is no possible doubt. A mistake was made. I am of the opinion that this wharf should be acquired by the government because the wharf we have built is of no use unless we make some arrangement with Mr. Shives. But 1 am at the same time of the opinion that $15,000 is a very high price indeed. I know

1171
the value of the work, I have been there, and I have declined to pay It myself.
Would an arbitration declare that price to be unreasonable ?

That I do not know. We are at the mercy of Mr. Skives. Before I left office I made a report suggesting that expropriation proceedings be taken. If we are compelled to pay $15,000, I suppose we shall have to pay it. In arbitration cases, the government usually does not get the best of it. All the same, I think an expropriation would be the safest course. Of course, my bon. friend may have new information since I left office.

No, the matter stands very much as my bon. friend left it. As my hon. friend from Leeds (Mr. Taylor) did not seem to think the information I gave was correct, I will say that I have no personal knowledge of the matter myself. I have had no personal interview with the owner and do not know him. The only information I have is what has been furnished to me by the department. It only came to me as a departmental matter. The information given to me by the department is that in 1880-90 a wharf 140 x 35 feet by some 35 feet in height was built at a distance of about 110 feet from the eastern end of the return at the outer end of Mowat's (formerly Ferguson's) wharf, the outer or channel faces of the said wharfs being kept in one and the same line ; the main object being to provide a place where vessels frequenting the Restigouehe river could conveniently deposit their ballast instead of throwing it into the river to the detriment of the harbour of Campbellton. In 1892-93 the ballast wharf, which is now about filled up, was connected by the Dominion government with Ferguson's or Mowat's (now Skives') wharf, by building up the gap between the two with cribwork, thus effecting a junction with the shore and the Intercolonial Railway, a branch line of which extends to Mowat's wharf. In the petition transmitted by Mr. McAllister, a supporter of the government at that time, on February 16th, 1896, the citizens of Campbellton represent that it is impossible to use the government ballast wharf as a landing pier without passing over Mowat's wharf, and that the charges for using the latter add considerably to the expense of the port, and they therefore ask the government to purchase the Mowat wharf and make it public property. That is a very concise and clear statement of the whole affair I as furnished by the department. I agree | with my hon. friend that it is in the public interest that we should purchase that pro-I perty. As to the price, when the matter came before me, I could not do anything about it until authorized by parliament. The sum named is the lowest price the owner would put on the property, and it is for the department to consider whether Hon. Mr. TARTE.
they will enter into an arrangement to take the property at that price, or expropriate it. I may say that our experience teaches us that if our own officials and experts in the valuation of properties consider that the price asked is not too high, I would prefer to purchase by agreement rather than go to court, because the probability Is that we would have a larger amount to pay and a great deal of costs. However, that may be, the passage of this vote does not at all preclude us from the right to arbitrate or expropriate if we think the price too high.

Mr. Skives and myself had several interviews. The reason Mr. Shives is asking so much is because he says he derives a yearly revenue of about $1,000 from his wharf. The wharf itself is not worth $15,000. I believe it is not worth more than perhaps $6,000 or $8,000. There is a valuation in the department by some of our officers to the effect that the work is not worth more than that and perhaps less. Mr. Shewen made a statement which was lower than that, but which I thought was too low. The fact remains that Mr. Shives is the owner of this piece of property, and is deriving a revenue of $1,000 from it every year, and he says, ' I do not see why I should be obliged to give you my property when lam getting so much out of it.' That is the real position of the matter.

This is giving a revenue of 1,000 and over and if we go to arbitration we will probably be stuck for a good deal more than we would be by an agreement because the courts as a, rule base the value on the revenue.
The hon. minister should bring down a plan before this item is voted.	'
If my hon. friend would agree to have an expropriation proceeding, the House might let the item go.
Is there any way of getting at the originators who built the wharf without getting the property ?

They have been punished.
Hon. Mr. ROSS (Victoria, N.S.) Mr. Shives asked $15,000 and the Minister of Public Works of that day, being a conscientious, honest man, refused to pay it. Now the government want a title to this property. Would it not be better at once to face the music and expropriate the property at once and be done with it ?

We will see later on.
Item allowed to stand.
Caraquet wharf, $55,000.
This is a large sum. Has the contract been let ?
Yes, this work is under contract. The contract was let in March, 1902.
Has any work been done and any money expended ?
No doubt.
The committee would like to know for what purpose this is required ?

No doubt parliament, when it authorized the vote, took full information and considered the matter fully. It is rather late now, after the money has been voted and the contract entered into, and the work under way and $10,000 already paid out, to stop the work.
When was the land purchased ? Last year we had the statement of the ex-Minister of Public Works that the land was not purchased and the site not finally located.
I do not find that we have to pay anything for the site.

Was the site given free ? There was trouble last year with regard to where the land was to be got and what we were going to pay for it, and the ex-Minister of Public Works said that before the contract was awarded he would see that the deed for the land was in his hands.
The contract was signed the 1st of March, 1902, long before that session was over.
For the purchase of the land ?
The property belongs to the Dominion. I do not see that there was any land to be purchased. $20 was the .cost of the right of way from the shore to the highway.

Last year Mr. Gan-ong asked the then Minister of Public Works (Hon. Mr. Tarte) who owned the land on which he was spending this money, and the answer was that it belonged to James Blackball. Does Mr. Blackball own the land or do we own it ?
I do not fmd anything in the memorandum of the department regarding the land except $20 for the right of way. That must be the land referred to.

The then Minister of Public Works said distinctly that Mr. James Blackball was the owner of the land.
The MINISTER OF , PUBLIC WORKS. He was merely referring to the right of way from the shore to the highway. That was conveyed to the Crown.
That is the right of way, but that is not where we are spending our money.

This parliament is entitled to a businesslike statement before we undertake work of this character. Here is an expenditure of $55,000 and if any hon. gentleman wants to know why it is being expended, there is nothing to show the reason. It is time that the department, when asking for money for any particular purpose, should come down in a businesslike way and state what public purpose the work is supposed to serve, what amount of money will be spent on it this year, and how much is the estimated cost. But we cannot get this information, and when we go out to the country we are told that we are to blame because we did not properly criticise these items. I know that the hon. the minister is new to the department and I am not hold-

ing him strictly responsible for this, but in the case of any new work a proper estimate should be brought down, and it is the duty of the opposition to refuse to allow any vote to go through uutil a full explanation is given.

No new work has been voted this session regarding which I have not given the fullest Information. As far as this work is concerned, it is now under contract. I am satisfied that no vote has gone through this session concerning which I have not given every detail. I think that parliament is entitled to this information, and I would not ask the House to vote any money unless I were prepared to give it. I think that is one principle that ought to be adhered to. Whatever tlje work is, it is the duty of parliament to make inquiries before committing itself to it. Parliament did commit itself to tliis work by giving a grant of money, and I suppose they received the information necessary at that time. The total estimated cost is $65,000.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
speechtext: This is under contract ?
Yes.
What is the present contract price ?
Why, then, does not the minister ask for the total cost of the work $05,000 ?
That is exactly what I am doing-$05,000 asked for this year, and $10,000 of last year's appropriation expended.
Who will own the wharf after it is built ?
The Dominion of Canada.
There must be something on the file which the minister has before him to prove who owns the land. Does Mr. Blackball own it or does the Dominion government own it ?
I have already explained that the government own it.
From whom did they purchase it ?
They purchased the right of way for $20. That is all the land we had to purchase, according to the information I have from the officers of the department.
Last year, when the then Minister of Public Works (Hon. Mr. Tarte) was asked: 'who owns the land?' he answered: 'Mr. James Blackball.' Surely nothing could be plainer than that.
On the information given me by the officer of the department I believe that refers to the right of way which, I have explained, we bought.	[DOT]

I may explain the circumstances. Of course the work is completed from the shore. But between the shore and the highway there is a small piece of land, and it is for that piece of land, 1 stated last year, $20 had to be paid. It is the right of way. No other property was purchased, it was not necessary to acquire any for the work itself, but only to acquire means of communication with the main road.
What is the size of the right of way ?
I have not at hand the description of the right of way. It is a small piece of land.
It goes through a piece of land of about an acre.
Has the piece of land been acquired by deed ?
Oh, oh.
The hon. member for Guysborough (Mr. Fraser) seems in a jocular mood Is he satisfied that the government lias the deed of the land ?

Most decidedly. The hon. gentleman might as well ask if the deed is signed or if there is a seal to it. The government own the foreshore, and all they needed was a piece of land from the street to the wharf. The minister says that the money was paid and the deed got and that the government own the land.
Did the hon. gentleman (Air. Fraser) hear that ?
Certainly I did.
Will the hon. minister say that now ?
He has said it.
AVill he say it now ?
The hon. minister as I understood him-
Oh, oh.

Just wait. Hon. gentlemen are like a jack in the box jumping up every minute. The hon. minister, as I understood him, stated that the Dominion government owned the place where the wharf was built that they needed a right of way from the street, and they bought it and got a deed of it. Is not that plain ? The deed specified the number of feet in the right of way and what difference does it make whether it is twenty or thirty feet ? I am bound to assume that they got the regular right of way.
Will the hon. minister tell us whether he has it or not ?

I am iuformed by the officials that we have.
Ij have given strict instructions that where we are doing work on property, the deed must be acquired, and, of course, I assume that the officials of the department will see to it that, in such a case as this, a proper right of way is acquired before the money is expended.
Great Salmon river-Groyne and breakwater combined, $4,300.
Where is this point ?
I move to strike out this item.
Will the hon. gentleman state why the item was put in the estimates ?

Representations were made that this was a necessary work, and I believe it is. But the property is reported by the department to be private property. I do not intend to ask for the money until this is arranged. If it is arranged, I can bring down a supplementary estimate. .

In what constituency is it?
The	MINISTER	OF	PUBLIC	WORKS.
St. John.

Motion agreed to.
Lord's Cove (Deer Island)-completion of [DOT]wharf, $500.

What amount has been expended on this wharf ?
The	MINISTER	OF	PUBLIC	"\yORKS.

Does the government own the approach to the wharf ?
The	MINISTER	OF	PUBLIC	WORKS.
Yes. This completes the work.
Richibucto, to complete protection and extension of north pier, &c., $2,500.
How long is this work ?

It is 703 feet in length. The amount of the contract was $22,900. Previous to this there has been spent on that work $155,000.
River St. John, including tributaries, $16,000. Mr.	WILMOT.	Will the minister give
some explanation of that vote ?
It has been customary to vote $16,000 for work on the St. John river. Last year $6,000 was spent, and this is a revote of $10,000 to make up the usual vote.

There is a great necessity for work being done there in the way of dredging, in order to facilitate navigation.
The traffic is very heavy and increasing, and the public suffers a good deal of inconvenience. I would especially direct attention to Oromocto Shoals.

I will see that everything is done there which we have means of doing.
River St. John and tributaries-to provide for contribution to local government, not to exceed one-half the first cost of wharfs built by them in tidal waters, $3,000.

This is the amount claimed by the provincial government under some old arrangement. The matter has been adjusted, but the Auditor General was not satisfied with the conditions on which the money was voted. This vote is asked for in order that we may pay the local government the sum due under the agreement made with them.

I had some trouble about sums of money previously placed in the estimates. The provincial government had built some small wharfs and then sent us the bill, asking us to pay half the cost.
I was never able to find out what kind of an agreement had taken place in former years ; but I remember that in 1899 or 1900 I wrote to the provincial Minister of Public Works telling him that unless the plans were submitted to the department previously to building their wharfs, we would not entertain the payment of that work. New Brunswick is the only province in which this government pays for work of that kind. I do not object, but I do not think it is a very good principle. I do not see why we should be obliged to help the provincial governments in building wharfs of that kind.
Will the minister explain on what principle it is that the Dominion government in this Instance is to provide one-half the cost and the local government to provide the other half ?
And we do not own the work.
Would the minister explain the peculiar circumstances which make it right for the Dominion government to pay one-half the cost of this work ?

An arrangement was made by the late government at the instance of the Hon. Mr. Foster, and agreed to by parliament, to vote one-half the cost of the work undertaken by the provincial government, on a certificate from the resident engineer that this work had been done at a fair price. As my hon. friend the ex-minister has explained, we took exception to this method. However, a vote of $5,000 was taken, but the Auditor General would not pay the money to New Brunswick, taking exception to the way the money was voted. This vote is asked for to carry out the obligation assumed

under that agreement. Since my hon. friend took exception to the method in which the account was rendered and the work was done, they have furnished us satisfactory evidence of the expenditure of the money on a certificate of the engineers, to the satisfaction of the department as well as of the Auditor General. We have to ask the revote of this money, and we do it in this way, so that it may be paid to the proper parties.

I really think we should not go on with such a practice. I took exception to it and the House will take exception to it with me, I am sure. X have seen these wharfs, they are very small wharfs, costing $300, $400 or $500. They are for local purposes and these works are very near to one another. I took exception to that kind of work. The record is there and it will show. I told them that in future I should not recommend to my colleagues the payment of one single dollar unless the plans of these wharfs were submitted to us. I suppose accounts that have been incurred in the past must be paid but I would suggest to my hon. friend not to allow that practice to be continued.

I must say that I am rather surprised with the argument made by the hon. Minister of Public Works that the practice should prevail with the present government because the Finance Minister of the government some seven years ago made certain arrangements. When so many arrangements made by the government have been completely upset why carry on this particular arrangement ?
Can the hon. gentleman (Mr. Brock) point out any obligation of the old government that this government has not carried out ?

Yes, I think I can remember some appointments to the Senate that were made by the late government that this government upset. What about the steamship service ? There is another point. The government of the Dominion are expending large amounts of money in the various provinces and, to keep to the items in the province of New Brunswick, there is an immense expenditure in that province for wharfs. I think we should go into the building of wharfs from a business point of view. I do not suppose the government build wharfs merely for political purposes but I take it for granted they are built because the business of the country requires it and if the business requires it the expenditure should have some kind of proportion to the amount that is earned by these wharfs. They should not spend money if it costs more to collect the tolls than the tolls amount to.
In these cases we do not collect any tolls because these wharfs are not our own property. We simply con- I
tribute the money towards these wharfs which is worse.

All the more reason why we should be careful in our expenditure of money, but even if we do get a revenue from it we should not expend $65,000 upon a wharf that probably will not bring in $500 a year of net revenue. Therefore, I contend this whole thing is wrong and I do not think anybody is more convinced of it than the Minister of Finance (Hon. Mr. Fielding) and the members of the government themselves, but they keep on and the reason given by the hon. Minister of Public Works is that this was a practice commenced by Mv. Foster the late minister of finance.
I never said that.
I understood the hon. minister to say that this was an arrangement made by Mr. Foster.

I was speaking of this particular arrangement with the provincial government which was made on the recommendation of Mr. Foster. It was adopted by the government of that day, approved of by parliament and the government in good faith expended this money. That is the reason I am asking parliament to pay it.

This government should not consider themselves bound to carry out any bad arrangement no matter by whom it is made. This is a very immoral and unbusinesslike arangement and it should be put a stop to at once.
A stop has been put to it. I- put a stop to it myself.
Why do we find it here still V

Because the amount that is placed in the estimates is to pay an old debt. This amount, I am sure, upon investigation, it will be proved is to pay debts that have been accumulating for four years. But, Sir. Foster never made any permanent arrangement so that in the future we are perfectly free.

It is hardly fair for the hon. member for Centre Toronto (Sir. Brock) to suggest that Sir. Foster made this arrangement for political purposes. I want to be fair to my predecessor in office and to defend him against this attack made upon him from the other side of the House.
I do not think the hon. gentleman is sincere.

Sir. Chairman, I do not see why the hon. gentlemen opposite should get their backs up because $3,000 is to be expended on the St. John river. The provin-

cial government have agreed to pay half of this expense, bnt I do not think they would be awfully put out if this government paid the whole of it. We have not had all the expenditure that we have asked for dredging and for wharfs in New Brunswick. I think the government should pay for some of this work and I think the hon. gentlemen opposite should be a little more lenient in their criticisms of items of this kind.

There is another point that we want to have cleared up before we carry this item. It is a matter that arises out of what the ex-Minister of Public Works (Hon. Mr. Tarte) said. The hon. gentleman gives us to understand that this is for the payment of an old debt, that is overdue some years, that it is not for something in the future, and therefore, if that is the case, I should like to have that explicit statement from the present hon. Minister of Public Works.

This is for an old debt for work already completed.
River St. John-wharf at Oromocto, $6,000.
I would like to know whether that work will be proceeded with at once '!

It is the intention of the department to proceed with this work at once. Tenders have been advertised for and the work will be commenced at once.
St. John harbour-Negro Point breakwater, $20,000.
What is the explanation of this V

This vote of $20,000 is to make good serious damage done to Negro Point breakwater ky storms, chiefly those of the 9th and 10th of November, 1900, the object being to save the lighthouse at the outer end of the breakwater which will certainly be destroyed if no steps are taken to rebuild its foundations in a more permanent manner with large blocks of granite and concrete. I may say to the Committee that I had an important deputation from the city of St. John making representations in reference to this breakwater. It seems from the representations of the leading citizens of that city that the harbour is almost useless without this breakwater and they are urging the expenditure of a very large sum for the purpose of extending it. There is some difference of opinion between the engineers as to how best to go on with this work. The total expenditure upon this breakwater up to the 30th of June last was $601,173. It is situated in a very bad place and the storms wash away the wood work frame. The work we are doing now is to
maintain the wharf and to protect the light house; it is of concrete and granite and will bo more durable.
Will this expenditure prevent the wharf from being washed away 1

Judging by the discussion I have had with the engineers and the deputation which waited on me, I am afraid I cannot guarantee that. The whole thing is a big work and will have to be considered most carefully.
Did the deputation suggest any kind of work that would be permanent ?
That was left an open question. They wanted the engineers to have a consultation and I have asked for a report.
Is it proposed to replace all the wood with concrete ?

The report in the department shows that it would cost at least $200,000 for a revetment of concrete to protect this work in a permanent way. It is estimated that it would cost $500,000 to carry out the work asked by the deputation which was to carry the breakwater clear across to Partridge Island. Some of the shipping people have taken objection to that and the matter will have to be gone into more carefully and a report made before I will recommend it to the House. This is for the maintenance of the existing work.
Is it to be done by contract ?
It would be Impossible to do this work in any other way than day labour.
It seems to me that this concrete work is usually done under contract.

This is repairing work and I do not think it would be possible for any engineer to make an estimate or specification. It is done under the direct supervision of Mr. Shewen, the engineer who has his headquarters in St. John. We would rather do it by contract if we could, because the present system takes up the time of our engineer and gives the department a great deal of trouble.
Do I understand that the minister is considering the advisability of closing up the western channel and extending the breakwater.
That has been suggested.
What will be the total cost of that work ?
I Nearly $500,000.
I know that a great many people in St. John are in favour of that being done.

And a great many objections are taken to it also.
St. John harbour-repairs and extension of protection work at base of Fort Dufferin, $3,500.

Last year the Minister of Public Works told us that a large dredge would this year be in operation in the harbour of St. John. There is now a great deal of difficulty experienced at the entrance of the harbour near the Beacon. Several delegations have awaited on the government urging the necessity of this work. What has become of the dredge that was promised ? Will it be at work this spring ?

My hon. friend (Hon. Mr. Tarte) was in good faith when he expected this dredge to be ready, but I cannot give any promise at the present time much as I regret it, seeing that there is such pressing work to be done. The dredge will not certainly be ready this season but we will take steps to have it completed as soon as possible.

Now that St. John harbour is becoming one of the great winter ports of the Dominion, it is urgent that that work should be done as soon as possible. Has the minister's attention been directed to dredging Grimross Canal, St. John river? This is an important work, and would not entail any great cost. I would strongly urge this work being carried out.
Shippegan harbour-repairs to protection work, &c., $1,100.
Was the money voted for this last year expended ?

This vote is to make provision in connection with a wharf 990 feet long reaching a depth of 31 feet 4 inches at low water. It is being built under contract. The amount of the contract is $12,000 and the total estimated cost $14,350. This will complete the work.
Is there a large amount of shipping at this place ?
It is a very important fishing centre in Gloucester county, New Brunswick.
Do anything but small boats go there ?
Boats of 14 and 15 tons.
I understood the minister to say that the depth of water was 14 feet.

The depth of water there is not necessary Hon. Mr. SUTHERLAND.
for the shipping, but the work being done in deep water it makes it more expensive.
Why has the hon. gentleman provided for a class of ships that do not go there ?

At this very wharf large ships have been coming since last fall, as well as a number of fishing boats.
